exposure: Antihypertensive medication changes (e.g., ACE inhibitors/ARBs replacement)
Preeclampsia screening methods (clinical risk markers, uterine artery pulsatility index, placental growth factor)
Dietary advice (for overweight/obese individuals at risk)
Timing of delivery (expectant care vs. initiation of delivery)
Postpartum blood pressure monitoring and evaluation
Interventions to reduce future pregnancy HDP risk and cardiovascular risk screening
outcome: Incidence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs)
Normalization of postpartum hypertension, clinical features, and laboratory tests
Risk of HDP in a future pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant women and women before or after pregnancy.
finding: This guideline provides comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations for the diagnosis, prediction, prevention, and management of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, including postpartum care.
mod_finding: Recommendations for platelet transfusion thresholds vary based on whether a vaginal or cesarean delivery is planned.
followup_time: At least 2 weeks postpartum for blood pressure measurement, with general guidance for ongoing postpartum care.
gest_age: Ranges from 11-14 weeks gestation for screening, up to 40+ weeks gestation for delivery timing, with specific recommendations for various gestational age windows (e.g., <34 weeks, 34-35+6 weeks, 36-36+6 weeks, 37+ weeks).
